doc.text: Every feature of a GeoJSON dataset: a URL (fetched and cached; `--refresh` fetches again) or a file path beside the profile. Each feature's `properties` become its tags, so `features.where` bands it by a number and `modules.labels({ keys })` names it:

const quakes = features.geojson("https://earthquake.usgs.gov/…/2.5_week.geojson")
features.where(quakes, { mag: { min: 6 } })

Or a GeoJSON object written in the profile (a graticule, a route, points of its own). Coordinates are lon/lat (RFC 7946); a point's third coordinate (a quake's depth) is the tag `geom:z`. In the browser a URL must allow CORS, and a file is one dropped on the page (by its name).

`clouds` — cumulus seen from above, heaped from puffs on a body that rises and falls, shaded where it turns from the sun or higher cloud shadows it. `spacing` is a puff's size; `coverage` the share of sky; `cell` the scale of the masses (default 8 puffs); `light_angle` (page degrees, default 225: from the top left) and `light_elevation` (default 30) the sun; `hatch` the shade's spacing at its deepest. `fills.cover` gives the clouds' footprint: mask what lies under them, and `areas.move` it down-sun for their shadow on the ground.

`clouds`: how far the masses are drawn out along `wind` (0–0.95). Default 0.25.
`clouds`: the wind's direction on the page, degrees. Default 15.

`growth`: roots this far apart, each draining its own basin. Default ~12× `spacing`.
`growth`: how much trees differ in size (0–1): uneven root spacing, big crowns next to saplings. Default 0.35.
`growth`: most pen passes on a trunk; thick near the roots, hairline at the twigs. Default 3.
`growth`: how far a branch advances per step, in mm. Default ~0.16× `spacing`.
`growth`: an attractor beyond this from every branch tip pulls nothing. Default ~3.2× `spacing`.
